title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 29, 2026: KOSPI -1.24%, KOSDAQ -2.34% as Czech Nuclear Talks Collapse
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,937.66, down 1.24%, and KOSDAQ closed at 753.23, down 2.34%, as profit-taking after the previous day's surge was compounded by the collapse of Czech nuclear construction talks. Individual themes moved on their own news: Marvell's reported pursuit of Lumentum lifted optical communication stocks, hopes for a Honam chip cluster lifted construction and infrastructure names, and space and satellite communication stocks were in focus.

1. KOSPI and KOSDAQ fall together — profit-taking after the surge

After surging the day before on strength in SK hynix and Samsung Electronics, Korean stocks corrected within a day. KOSPI fell to 5,937.66 (-1.24%) and KOSDAQ to 753.23 (-2.34%). Profit-taking followed the previous day's jump, expectations faded after Samsung Electronics' earnings release, and the breakdown of Czech nuclear construction talks and pressure from a battery-related stake deal added to the cautious mood.

2. Marvell reportedly pursues Lumentum — AI optical communication stocks in focus

News said U.S. chip company Marvell Technology is pursuing an acquisition of optical components maker Lumentum Holdings. Lumentum's value was cited at about $83 billion, roughly 115 trillion won. If the deal goes through, expectations are that the combined business would be stronger in optical communication, a key part of AI data center infrastructure. As AI data centers move large volumes of data quickly, optical components and laser technology matter more. Gwangjeonja, RF Materials and Bitsaem Electronics (빛샘전자) were in focus, and RF Materials drew attention for its pump laser package business for optical communication. The pursuit is a reported stage only, so whether it is completed and its real effect on Korean companies should be checked.

3. Hopes for a Honam chip cluster — construction and infrastructure stocks in focus

Hopes for a semiconductor cluster in the Honam region spread to regional construction and infrastructure stocks. If a chip industrial complex is built, demand for civil works, infrastructure and construction materials could rise. Seosan and Kumho Electric were named in the theme, and Dongyang Pile drew interest on expectations for construction infrastructure investment. Direct participation or new supply contracts have not been confirmed for these companies, so the moves should be read as theme-driven buying on regional development hopes.

4. Czech Dukovany nuclear talks collapse — nuclear and construction stocks plunge

Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power said it is ending construction contract talks with a consortium of Daewoo E&C and Doosan Enerbility over the Dukovany nuclear project in the Czech Republic. The sides could not close gaps over how to settle construction costs, contract terms and responsibility sharing, and KHNP plans to start a process to select a new contractor. Daewoo E&C and Doosan Enerbility fell by double digits during the session, and selling spread across nuclear-related stocks on worries about schedule delays, higher project costs and uncertainty over follow-up contracts.

The collapse of the construction talks does not mean the Czech nuclear project as a whole is cancelled. KHNP is continuing the project and preparing to select a new contractor, and some contracts, including Doosan Enerbility's reactor and turbine equipment supply contracts, were signed separately. Uncertainty from ending the construction talks should be separated from the status of the project overall.

5. Space and satellite communication stocks — Contec, HVM and AP Satellite in focus

Contec builds and operates satellite ground stations, and its record of sending and receiving satellite data through its own ground station and of a low-earth-orbit satellite optical communication demonstration drew attention. Expanding satellite communication infrastructure and expectations for space industry growth supported sentiment. AP Satellite, which makes satellite communication terminals and related systems, was also in focus, and HVM, which works in advanced metals and special alloy materials used in aerospace and defense, was mentioned on expectations of rising materials demand.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Oct 29?
KOSPI fell 1.24% to 5,937.66 and KOSDAQ fell 2.34% to 753.23, with profit-taking after the previous day's surge.

Has the Czech nuclear project been cancelled?
No. KHNP ended construction contract talks with the Daewoo E&C and Doosan Enerbility consortium but is continuing the project and plans to select a new contractor. Doosan Enerbility's reactor and turbine supply contracts were signed separately.

Do all Honam chip cluster stocks benefit directly?
No. Direct participation or new supply contracts have not been confirmed; the moves reflect theme-driven buying on regional development hopes.
